questions.question: 77412. মানবদেহে ইনসুলিন হরমোন নিঃসৃত হয় কোন গ্রন্থি থেকে?
questions.explain:
• সঠিক উত্তর: খ) অগ্ন্যাশয়।

• অগ্ন্যাশয় ও ইনসুলিন:
- অগ্ন্যাশয়ের ল্যাঙ্গারহ্যান্সের দ্বীপের বিটা কোষ থেকে ইনসুলিন হরমোন নিঃসৃত হয়।
- ইনসুলিন রক্তে গ্লুকোজের মাত্রা নিয়ন্ত্রণ করে।
- ইনসুলিনের অভাবে ডায়াবেটিস মেলিটাস হতে পারে।

• অন্যান্য অপশন:
ক) থাইরয়েড — থাইরক্সিন হরমোন নিঃসরণ করে।
গ) পিটুইটারি — একে প্রধান বা মাস্টার গ্রন্থি বলা হয়।
ঘ) অ্যাড্রিনাল — অ্যাড্রেনালিনসহ বিভিন্ন হরমোন নিঃসরণ করে।

উৎস: জীববিজ্ঞান, নবম-দশম শ্রেণি।

questions.question: 77411. Vincent's symptom in mandibular osteomyelitis refers to:
questions.option3: Lower lip paresthesia due to inferior alveolar nerve involvement
questions.explain: Vincent's symptom is paresthesia (numbness or altered sensation) of the lower lip and chin caused by involvement of the inferior alveolar nerve (IAN) in mandibular osteomyelitis.

questions.question: 77410. Which cervical lymph nodes are primarily enlarged in an acute infection involving the mandibular molars?
questions.explain: Most mandibular posterior teeth drain to the submandibular lymph nodes.

questions.question: 77409. In a patient with thrombocytopenia, spontaneous oral bleeding is most likely when the platelet count falls below:
questions.explain: Spontaneous mucosal bleeding becomes common below 20,000 platelets/mm³.

questions.question: 77408. During incision and drainage of a fluctuant buccal space abscess, the incision should be placed:
questions.option1: At the highest point of swelling
questions.option4: At the most dependent part of the abscess
questions.explain: Dependent drainage promotes continuous evacuation of pus and prevents reaccumulation.

questions.question: 77407. Which cranial nerve is most commonly affected first in cavernous sinus thrombosis?
questions.explain: CN VI lies freely within the cavernous sinus and is usually affected first.

questions.question: 77406. Which fascial space infection most commonly causes severe trismus?
questions.explain: Involvement of the muscles of mastication causes marked limitation of mouth opening.

questions.question: 77405. Which clinical feature helps differentiate cellulitis from an abscess?
questions.explain: Cellulitis causes a diffuse, hard (indurated) swelling, whereas an abscess is localized and fluctuant.

questions.question: 77404. A patient taking warfarin requires tooth extraction. Which laboratory test should be checked before surgery?
questions.explain: Warfarin inhibits vitamin K-dependent clotting factors (II, VII, IX, X). Its anticoagulant effect is monitored using PT/INR, not aPTT.

questions.question:
77403. A patient has persistent numbness of the lower lip after surgical removal of an impacted mandibular third molar, but tongue sensation is normal.
Which nerve has most likely been injured?
questions.explain: The inferior alveolar nerve provides sensation to the lower lip via the mental nerve.

questions.question:
77402. A patient with uncontrolled diabetes develops persistent jaw pain, swelling, fever, and a draining sinus 3 weeks after extraction. Radiographs reveal a moth-eaten appearance with a sequestrum.
The diagnosis -
questions.explain: Chronic osteomyelitis presents with sequestrum formation, draining sinus, and characteristic radiographic changes.

questions.question: 77401. Which of the following is NOT a feature of acute pericoronitis-
questions.option2: Pain around a partially erupted tooth
questions.option4: Maxillary 3rd molar is most commonly affected
questions.explain:
Acute pericoronitis is an acute infection and inflammation of the soft tissue (operculum) surrounding the crown of a partially erupted tooth, most commonly the Mandibular third molar.
Features:
Severe, throbbing pain around the partially erupted tooth
Swollen, red, and tender operculum
Pus discharge from beneath the operculum on pressure
Bad taste in the mouth and halitosis (bad breath)
Pain on chewing and difficulty eating
Trismus (restricted mouth opening) due to inflammation of masticatory muscles
Dysphagia (difficulty swallowing) in severe cases
Fever and malaise
Tender, enlarged submandibular lymph nodes
Difficulty maintaining oral hygiene because of pain

questions.question: 77400. Persistent bleeding after tooth extraction despite a normal platelet count suggests:
questions.explain:
Hemophilia A is an X-linked recessive bleeding disorder caused by Factor VIII deficiency.
Platelet count is normal, because the disorder affects coagulation factors, not platelets.
The patient has impaired secondary hemostasis, so the initial platelet plug forms, but the fibrin clot is unstable.
As a result, bleeding after dental extraction may persist for hours or recur after initially stopping.
Laboratory findings
✅ Platelet count: Normal
✅ Bleeding time (BT): Normal
✅ Prothrombin time (PT): Normal
✅ Activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT): Prolonged

A. Leukemia: May cause prolonged bleeding due to thrombocytopenia, but the platelet count is often low or abnormal, not normal.
C. Thrombocytopenia: Causes bleeding because of a low platelet count, which contradicts the question.
D. Polycythemia: Involves increased red blood cell mass and is not a typical cause of persistent post-extraction bleeding.

questions.question: 77399. Which symptom is most characteristic of irreversible acute pulpitis?
questions.option3: Spontaneous, lingering pain, especially at night
questions.explain: Irreversible pulpitis typically causes spontaneous, severe, throbbing pain that lingers after the stimulus is removed.

questions.question:
77398. A 45-year-old diabetic man presents with severe mandibular pain, facial swelling, fever, and pus discharge 1 week after extraction of a mandibular molar. Radiograph shows irregular areas of bone destruction.
What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explain:
Acute osteomyelitis presents with:
Severe pain
Swelling
Fever
Pus discharge
Bone destruction on radiographs
The mandible is affected more commonly than the maxilla because of its relatively poorer blood supply.

questions.question: 77397. Which jaw is more commonly affected by osteomyelitis?
questions.explain: The mandible has a denser cortical plate and a relatively poorer blood supply than the maxilla, making it more susceptible.

questions.question: 77396. A patient complains of severe pain 48 hours after extraction. Examination reveals loss of the blood clot but no pus formation or facial swelling.what is the most likely diagnosis.
questions.explain:
Alveolar osteitis:(Dry socket)
The classic triad is:
Pain starting 2–4 days after extraction
Empty socket with exposed bone
Foul odor/bad taste
This is typical of dry socket.

questions.question: 77395. A patient has a non-vital mandibular first molar with swelling and pus at the apex. The diagnosis is:
questions.explain:
Periapical abscess is an acute or chronic localized suppurative infection at the apex of a non-vital tooth resulting from pulpal necrosis.
A periapical abscess develops due to infection from a non-vital tooth.

questions.question: 77394. Infection commonly spreads to the buccal space from which teeth?
questions.explain:
The buccal space lies between the buccinator muscle and the overlying skin/fascia. Infection spreads into this space when the cortical plate is perforated above (maxilla) or below (mandible) the attachment of the buccinator muscle.
Maxillary premolars and first molars commonly drain into the buccal space.
Mandibular first molars are the most common mandibular source because the buccal root apices often lie below the buccinator attachment, allowing infection to enter the buccal space.

questions.question: 77393. A patient develops buccal space infection following a maxillary molar abscess. Which structure within the buccal space acts as a barrier to the spread of infection into the lateral pharyngeal space?
questions.explain: The buccal fat pad acts as an impediment to the spread of infection from the buccal space to the lateral pharyngeal space.

questions.question: 77392. Which finding is best differentiate an acute periodontal abscess from an acute periapical abscess -
questions.explain: The affected tooth in a periodontal abscess is usually vital, whereas a periapical abscess is associated with pulp necrosis.

questions.question: 77391. Which structure is found within the pterygomandibular space?
questions.explain:
Structures lying in the pterygomandibular space:
Inferior alveolar nerve (before it enters the mandibular foramen)
Inferior alveolar artery
Inferior alveolar vein
Lingual nerve (lies anterior and medial to the inferior alveolar nerve)
Sphenomandibular ligament
Loose areolar connective tissue and fat
These structures are clinically important during nerve blocks.

questions.question: 77390. Which radiographic finding indicates healing of osteomyelitis?
questions.explain: As infection resolves, bone density increases, resulting in progressive sclerosis, which indicates healing.

questions.question: 77389. Which radiographic sign is associated with Garre's osteomyelitis-
questions.explain: Garre's osteomyelitis causes repeated subperiosteal new bone formation, resulting in the classic onion-skin appearance on X-ray.

questions.question: 77388. Most common causative organism of osteomyelitis is-
questions.explain: Staphylococcus aureus is the commonest pathogen.

questions.question:
77387. A 45-year-old patient with chronic periodontitis develops a painful swelling beside the mandibular first molar. The tooth is vital, and pus drains through a deep periodontal pocket.
What is the diagnosis?
questions.explain: A periodontal abscess originates from a periodontal pocket, and the affected tooth is usually vital, unlike a periapical abscess.

questions.question: 77386. Which tooth is commonly associated with both buccal & palatal abcess?

questions.question: 77385. Cavernous sinus thrombosis is most commonly caused by infection from:
questions.explain: The danger area of the face (upper lip, nose, maxillary canine region) drains through the facial and angular veins into the cavernous sinus via the superior ophthalmic vein. Because these veins are valveless, infection can spread retrogradely, causing CST.

questions.question: 77371. The average total length of the maxillary canine is approximately:
questions.explain:
Average total length is about 26.5 mm.
The average total length of an adult human tooth—from the visible tip (crown) to the root embedded in the jawbone—ranges from 19 to 25 mm (0.75 to 1 inch). 
Total lengths vary depending on the specific tooth type: 
Incisors (Front teeth): 22–23 mm
Canines (Pointed teeth): 25–26.5mm
Premolars: 20–23 mm
Molars (Back teeth): 19–22 mm

questions.question: 77370. Approximately how long is the average maxillary central incisor (crown + root)?
questions.explain: The maxillary central incisor has an Around 22.5 mm total length of approximately 22.5 mm. It is longer than the mandibular central incisor but shorter than the maxillary canine. This length, combined with its wide mesio-distal dimension, contributes to its overall prominent size among incisors.

questions.question: 77369. The cervical constriction (narrowing at the neck of the tooth) in deciduous teeth is:
questions.option1: Less pronounced than in permanent teeth
questions.option2: More pronounced than in permanent teeth
questions.explain: Deciduous teeth show a more pronounced cervical constriction compared to permanent teeth. This gives primary molars a more bulbous crown shape that narrows sharply near the cervical region. It is a classic feature used to visually distinguish deciduous molars from their permanent successors.

questions.question: 77368. Which anomaly is considered most important before endodontic treatment of mandibular first molars?
questions.explain:
An extra distolingual root may be missed during treatment.
Failure to detect it can cause endodontic failure.
Radiographic examination is essential.

questions.question: 77367. Which developmental anomaly is known as "tooth within a tooth"?
questions.explain:
Dens invaginatus results from invagination of enamel into the dental papilla.
It creates the appearance of a "tooth within a tooth."
It is commonly seen in maxillary lateral incisors.

questions.question: 77366. Extra or bifurcated canals in mandibular premolars are reported more frequently in:
questions.explain:
Studies show a higher frequency of extra canals in African-descent populations.
Elevated rates are also reported in Turkish, Kuwaiti, and Chinese groups.
This has important endodontic implications.

questions.question: 77365. Enamel pearls are commonly found:
questions.option3: Near the furcation of mandibular first molars
questions.option4: Near the furacation of maxillary 1st premolar
questions.explain:
Enamel pearls are ectopic enamel nodules.
They usually occur near the furcation.
They may predispose to periodontal problems.

questions.question: 77364. The mixed dentition period extends approximately from:
questions.explain:
Mixed dentition contains both primary and permanent teeth.
It begins with the eruption of the first permanent molar.
It ends when the last primary tooth exfoliates.

questions.question: 77363. Shovel-shaped incisors are most commonly found in:
questions.explain:
Shovel-shaped morphology is most frequently observed in maxillary central incisors.
It may also occur in maxillary lateral incisors.
It is uncommon in mandibular incisors.
